title: Cut and publish 0.6.1 carrying the LCLI-474 log.md fix
description:
Cut and publish 0.6.1, carrying LCLI-474 (lore sync destroys log.md entries it cannot
re-derive). Authorized by the user on 2026-09-11 after the orchestrator established that
every fleet session runs the published npm binary, so the fix reaches nobody until it
ships. quest-cli's standing ruling to hand-revert its log.md on every sync stays in force
until this release is on npm.

SCOPE: 0.6.0 -> 0.6.1, a single-purpose patch. dev was level with main before this work,
and Unreleased holds exactly one entry, so the release carries the LCLI-474 fix, the
LCLI-473 tracker record, and nothing else.

The bump is not a version string. Per docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md it is ONE commit
containing all of:
- seven package.json versions (root + six npm/<platform>/) AND the root's six
  optionalDependencies pins. release.yml's verify-versions job gates build on all seven
  plus the pin and the license/author/repository metadata.
- .claude-plugin/plugin.json's version. 0.4.3 shipped without this and the marketplace pin
  moving to v0.4.3 still resolved as 0.4.2 everywhere, because Claude Code reads
  plugin.json's own version, not the git tag.
- bun.lock regenerated with the PINNED Bun from .bun-version (1.3.14; the local toolchain
  matches, verified). A lockfile still resolving the previous version fails
  --frozen-lockfile in setup-bun and kills every CI job before any gate runs. The trap is
  that it does not fail at bump time -- the new platform packages do not exist on the
  registry yet, so the drift is invisible until publication makes the pins resolvable
  (LCLI-369).
- three Ladybug digest baselines, which move because the canonical export embeds
  lore/<version> as provenance. Only canonicalExportSha256 may move; if
  sourceInventorySha256 or taskSnapshotSha256 also moved, that is a code regression
  wearing a version bump's commit message. A negative control (revert only the root
  version, expect the OLD baselines to pass) proves the change is version-driven.
- README install commands stay versionless, and docs/reference/lore-cli-release-truth.md is
  the ONE file in docs/ carrying the current published version. The grep sweep for
  '@opum-ai/lore@[0-9]' must return only its two pinned historical exemptions.

THEN: promote dev to main (PR, full main matrix on that exact SHA, then git push origin
dev:main -- never the merge button), tag the verified commit, dispatch Release with
publish: false, and publish THAT RUN'S npm-packages artifact via
scripts/publish-release.sh -- platform packages first, root last, never a locally rebuilt
tarball.

TWO STEPS NEED THE USER DIRECTLY and are batched into one ask rather than trickled: the
annotated tag (git tag -a is classifier-denied in this session) and the npm publish itself.
Both are irreversible; a published version cannot be unpublished, only deprecated.

DOWNSTREAM OBLIGATION, easy to forget because nothing in this repo fails without it:
opum-marketplace's check-federated-content.mjs asserts the federated skills/ bytes match a
baseline resolved from the tag. A new tag without telling opum-marketplace the resolved
skills/ SHA turns its check red.

acceptanceCriteria.text: All seven package.json versions, the six optionalDependencies pins, and .claude-plugin/plugin.json read 0.6.1, in one commit
bun.lock regenerated with the Bun pinned in .bun-version, and `bun install --frozen-lockfile` exits 0 with its exit code taken unpiped
The three Ladybug digest baselines are refreshed, and the change is PROVEN version-driven: only canonicalExportSha256 moved, and the negative control returns to passing against the old baselines
The docs sweep for '@opum-ai/lore@[0-9]' returns only its two pinned historical exemptions; release-truth carries the new version and no other file grew a current-state claim
dev is promoted to main by fast-forward (git push origin dev:main) after the full matrix is green on that exact SHA, never via the merge button
The tag points at the verified commit, and Release is dispatched with publish: false on it

The seven published tarballs are the workflow run's own npm-packages artifact, sha256-verified by scripts/publish-release.sh before any registry write, platform packages first and the root package last
opum-marketplace is told the resolved skills/ SHA for the new tag, so its federated-content check does not go red
quest-cli is told when 0.6.1 is on npm, since its ruling to hand-revert log.md stands until then

- A separate quest-cli investigation (git operations SIGKILLed on a freshly built

comments.body:
SESSION 2026-09-13 (late). Publish still blocked, but the blocker is now NAMED rather than suspected, and two of the three prerequisites are closed.

1) THE "CANNOT FIND THE COMMIT" MESSAGE IS NOT A TRUST PROBLEM. The user hit it while updating the Trusted Publisher for @opum-ai/lore-darwin-arm64 and asked whether the update worked. It is unrelated. Every already-published version carries SLSA provenance pinning a commit the 2026-09-10 repo delete/recreate destroyed: 0.6.0's attestation resolves to gitCommit 59ba30e497f8e98aa6c6be022d9363fd718fb4ee at refs/tags/v0.6.0, and GitHub now answers 422 "No commit found for SHA" for it. Its build run 34393976910 is 404 too. The SHA still resolves in the local clone's loose objects, which is exactly why this looks fine locally and broken on npmjs.com -- do not "verify" it with git cat-file and conclude nothing is wrong. Nothing repairs the existing links short of republishing. quest-cli confirmed the identical shape across all 8 of its pre-0.6.1 versions, same root cause; QCLI-267 already shipped the documented-not-repaired response (a GitHub Release plus a --pre/--post provenance gate in release.yml). lore-cli has no equivalent gate yet -- worth its own task, NOT worth bolting onto this release.

2) TRUST REGISTRATION STATE, from the user directly: darwin-arm64 only. The other six are not registered. The remaining six are lore-darwin-x64, lore-linux-arm64, lore-linux-x64, lore-win32-arm64, lore-win32-x64, and the root @opum-ai/lore. Fields are in docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md's current-state table (org opum-ai, repo lore-cli, workflow filename release.yml, allowed action npm publish, Environment release) -- all case-sensitive, and npm does not validate on save.

DO NOT DISPATCH publish:true UNTIL ALL SEVEN ARE REGISTERED. Both the OIDC publish job and scripts/publish-release.sh fail closed mid-loop, platform packages first and root launcher last. One registered package therefore publishes lore-darwin-arm64@0.6.1 and then 404s, leaving an unretractable partial family with no root launcher. npm unpublish is heavily restricted. This is the single most expensive mistake available tonight.

3) LOCAL CREDENTIAL: the user ran npm login, and npm whoami now returns jeremy-newhouse. That fixes the earlier 401 but does NOT give a read path to the trust config: npm trust list demands a fresh browser OTP per call, and in a non-TTY npm redacts the auth URL to *** (confirmed in its own debug log), so an agent session cannot complete the flow. Seven browser round-trips in a real terminal is the only CLI route. Asking the user what they registered is cheaper and was the right call.

4) THE RELEASE ENVIRONMENT GATE IS NOW REAL -- this contradicts the previous handoff note in this task, which said "both currently have ZERO protection rules". That was inherited from LCLI-278's description rather than re-read from the API. gh api repos/opum-ai/lore-cli/environments/release now shows a required_reviewers rule (id 65483841, jeremy-newhouse). Full evidence and the updated_at dating trap are recorded on LCLI-278, whose three acceptance criteria are now checked; it stays open only until the dispatch is observed to actually pause.

5) DOCS FIXED THIS SESSION, on branch docs/LCLI-278-release-env-verified: release-publishing.md's current-state section claimed the release environment "still has no protection rules and administrator bypass, so a dispatch has no second-party approval". False as of today. Replaced with the dated, evidenced version plus the two residual caveats (can_admins_bypass, and the npm-side Environment claim being what makes the rule binding). lore check exits 0. A false alarm worth not repeating: the five/six package counts at lines 259-302 are the 0.1.0 bootstrap HISTORY and are correct -- win32-arm64 postdates 0.1.0. The current-state section already says seven. Do not "fix" those.

NEXT ACTION: user registers the remaining six, says so, then dispatch gh workflow run release.yml --repo opum-ai/lore-cli --ref v0.6.1 -f publish=true. Watch that the publish job pauses for environment approval (that observation closes LCLI-278). Tag v0.6.1 -> 20a1d24b and green qualification run 34783940117 are both unchanged and still valid; dev and main are level at 20a1d24b.

LOCAL SHIM STILL IN PLACE and still required -- see the previous handoff note. Confirmed working again this session: lore sync added exactly one line to docs/log.md (329 -> 330) instead of collapsing it, which is the LCLI-474 fix behaving correctly. Remove the shim only once 0.6.1 is actually on npm.

ROOT CAUSE OF THE OIDC PUBLISH FAILURE, proven 2026-09-13. Not a trust registration problem,
not a token problem, and not fixable by re-registering anything.

GitHub issues IMMUTABLE-FORMAT OIDC subject claims for this repository, and npm's Trusted
Publishing does not match them.

PROOF, not inference. A throwaway probe workflow (branch chore/oidc-probe, since deleted; run
34787200768) requested id-token: write, minted a real token with audience npm:registry.npmjs.org,
and decoded the payload:

  SUB=repo:opum-ai@311910387/lore-cli@1365013937:ref:refs/heads/chore/oidc-probe
  AUD=npm:registry.npmjs.org
  REPO=opum-ai/lore-cli   REPO_ID=1365013937

npm expects the classic `repo:opum-ai/lore-cli:...`. The publish job is scoped to
`environment: release`, so it presents `repo:opum-ai@311910387/lore-cli@1365013937:environment:release`
where npm wants `repo:opum-ai/lore-cli:environment:release`. No match, so npm treats the request
as unauthenticated and answers E404 on PUT -- indistinguishable from a missing trust relationship.
npm/cli#9088 is other people hitting exactly this ambiguity.

WHY NOW, and it IS the repo recreation after all. GitHub's changelog "Immutable subject claims for
GitHub Actions OIDC tokens" (2026-04-23) states every repository created after 2026-07-15
automatically uses the new format, delimiter `@`. lore-cli was deleted and recreated 2026-09-10
(OPAG-70), which made it a new repository. 0.6.0 published successfully from CI on 2026-09-09 --
ONE DAY EARLIER, under the old repo id and the classic subject. quest-cli was recreated the same
hour and is broken identically.

A REASONING TRAP THAT COST THIS SESSION TWO WRONG CONCLUSIONS, worth reading before repeating it:
I checked opum-doc, lore-web and opum-marketplace, found use_immutable_subject: true on all of
them, and concluded the recreation could not be the cause since those were never recreated. That
was invalid -- every repo in this org was created after the 2026-07-15 cutoff (earliest is lore-web
at 2026-07-28), so they were never a control group. Check the CUTOFF DATE, not whether a repo was
recreated.

A SECOND FALSE LEAD, same session: the publish job's "GITHUB_TOKEN Permissions" log group prints
only `Contents: read` and `Metadata: read` even when id-token IS granted. I read that absence as
the root cause and nearly reported it. The probe disproved it -- the token minted fine. Do not
infer a missing id-token permission from that log group.

WHAT CANNOT FIX IT:
- Re-registering Trusted Publishers. The user registered all seven; the E404 is unchanged.
- Repo-level opt-out. `PUT /repos/opum-ai/lore-cli/actions/oidc/customization/sub` with
  use_immutable_subject:false is ACCEPTED (returns {}) and has NO EFFECT -- read-back still true.
  A custom include_claim_keys template applies but the immutable prefix persists regardless.
  Both were tried and reverted; the repo is back to use_default:true.
- GitHub documents no opt-out once adopted, and npm's docs never mention the format at all.

ORG-LEVEL was not attempted: this session's permission classifier blocked the write as
"Security Weaken". That is the correct gate -- it is the user's decision, not an agent's.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RELEASE PROCESS: release.yml's publish job cannot work until npm supports
immutable subjects. Every lore release must use the manual path (scripts/publish-release.sh)
until then. That is a regression in the release mechanism, not in the product, and it deserves
its own task rather than living only in this note.

MANUAL PATH ALSO NEEDS A HUMAN: scripts/publish-release.sh gets EOTP -- npm demands a browser
one-time password per publish, and in a non-TTY npm redacts the auth URL to ***. An agent session
cannot complete it. Verified tonight: the script stopped at the first package, published nothing,
and all seven remained 0.6.0. Its fail-closed ordering (platform first, root launcher last) worked
exactly as designed.

LATER CORRECTION, appended 2026-09-13, ORIGINAL TEXT DELIBERATELY LEFT INTACT ABOVE.

This record is Done and stays as written -- rewriting a completed record to remove a word falsifies it. But one sentence in the root-cause comment above has since been shown to overreach, and a reader who finds this record first should not carry it away uncorrected:

    "quest-cli was recreated the same hour and is broken identically."

The recreation timing is right. "Broken identically" was asserted from a shared E404 symptom without quest-cli's evidence, and it propagated into LCLI-482 and from there into a cross-repo claim that took three sessions to unwind. quest-cli separately reached a DIFFERENT (and also wrong) root cause of their own; both were strong inferences with the last step left unclosed. LCLI-482 carries the reconciliation, the npm-source disproof, and the corrected wording.

WHAT SURVIVES UNCHANGED, and is if anything better supported now: the immutable-subject finding for THIS repo, the probe-run token decode, the two documented false leads, and -- newly relevant -- "Re-registering Trusted Publishers. The user registered all seven; the E404 is unchanged." That line is an experiment, and it is what excludes the simplest competing explanation for lore-cli. It is the most load-bearing sentence in this record and nobody noticed at the time.

WHAT IS STILL NOT ESTABLISHED: why npm's exchange actually refused. oidc.js swallows that reason at anything below verbose. Read it as "confirmed subject format, inferred refusal cause" until someone dispatches with NPM_CONFIG_LOGLEVEL=verbose (landed in #18) and reads the line.

finalSummary:
RELEASED 2026-09-13. All seven @opum-ai/lore* packages are live on npm at 0.6.1 with latest moved on each, verified against the registry and by the script's own clean-room npx install (fresh temp dir, nothing from local caches) returning 0.6.1.

HOW IT ACTUALLY SHIPPED, which is NOT what this task assumed. AC#5 anticipated a publish:true dispatch doing the work. That dispatch (run 34786808767) failed, and 0.6.1 was published MANUALLY via scripts/publish-release.sh 0.6.1 34783940117 against run 34783940117's own npm-packages artifact, every tarball sha256-verified against SHA256SUMS.txt before any registry write, platform packages first and the root launcher last. AC#6 is therefore satisfied exactly as written -- the published bytes are a qualified workflow run's own artifact, digest-checked -- even though the mechanism differed.

THE COST, stated plainly because it is a real regression and not a footnote: 0.6.1 CARRIES NO PROVENANCE ATTESTATION, where 0.6.0 did. Provenance is produced by the CI OIDC path, and that path is broken. Anyone comparing versions will find signed SLSA provenance on 0.6.0 and none on 0.6.1.

WHY OIDC FAILED, proven rather than inferred, and filed as LCLI-482. GitHub issues immutable-format OIDC subject claims for this repository -- repo:opum-ai@311910387/lore-cli@1365013937:... -- and npm Trusted Publishing matches the classic repo:opum-ai/lore-cli:... form, so npm treats the token as unauthenticated and answers E404 on PUT. Established by decoding a real token minted with audience npm:registry.npmjs.org in probe run 34787200768. Per GitHub's 2026-04-23 changelog every repository created after 2026-07-15 uses this format; lore-cli was deleted and recreated 2026-09-10, ONE DAY AFTER 0.6.0 published successfully over this same OIDC path. That one-day gap is the cleanest evidence available. Re-registering Trusted Publishers does not help -- all seven were re-registered before the attempt -- and there is no repo-level opt-out.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, all nine met:
1-3. Version bump, lockfile and Ladybug baselines: landed earlier, unchanged.
4. Docs sweep: README now reads 0.6.1 and release-truth carries a 0.6.1 Current state section. NOTE, more honest than the AC's wording: the sweep returns THREE historical references outside release-truth, not two -- research/2026-08-12.../00-primary-source-verification.md, docs/adr/0020, and release-publishing.md's 0.1.0 bootstrap line. All three are accurate history and none is a current-state claim. The AC's "two" was already stale when written.
5. dev promoted to main by fast-forward at 20a1d24b, full matrix green, never the merge button.
6. Tag v0.6.1 -> 20a1d24b; publish:false run 34783940117 green on that exact commit.
7. Published bytes are that run's own artifact, sha256-verified, platform-first root-last. See above re mechanism.
8. opum-marketplace told the resolved skills/ tree SHA 24277e9a94d6cc9b5a8c7fa12fa32c4f15eb4c0f for tag v0.6.1.
9. quest-cli told 0.6.1 is on npm, with the full manual-publish procedure, since their release is blocked by the identical cause.

SIDE RESULT WORTH KEEPING: LCLI-278 closed on this release. Its required-reviewer gate was not merely present but observed to FIRE -- run 34786808767 went to status 'waiting', pending_deployments named env=release and approver jeremy-newhouse, nothing reached npm while it sat, and it resumed only on approval. Do not read that run's overall 'failure' conclusion as the gate failing; the gate worked and the npm step after it did not.

LOCAL SHIM REMOVED, as this task's own handoff instructed. npm install -g @opum-ai/lore@0.6.1 replaced the frozen-source shim with the real published binary; bin/lore is a symlink again, lore --version reports 0.6.1 from the published package, lore check exits 0, and docs/log.md is intact at 330 lines. The frozen copy under ~/.claude/local-shims/ is now unused and can be deleted whenever convenient.
